paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is shouting: seek the LORD BEFORE the day arrives, not after. Zephaniah says it three times in one verse, "before the decree takes effect," "before the burning anger of the LORD comes upon you," "before the Day of the LORD’s anger comes upon you" (Zephaniah 2:2). He calls the humble to "Seek the LORD," to seek righteousness and humility (Zephaniah 2:3). And I'll say it plain: waiting until the timer goes off is a terrible time to start looking for the oven mitts.

Now look at what ties the nations together. Moab and the Ammonites were proud and taunted the LORD's people (Zephaniah 2:8, 10). Nineveh thought to herself, "I am it, and there is none besides me" (Zephaniah 2:15). Pride says, "I've got this, nobody can touch me." But the LORD of Hosts is not impressed by that, friend, and no wall, no army and no cedar beams are going to argue with Him.

And here's the part that makes me want to dance on my gold base. The same LORD who brings down the proud also looks after His people: He will "attend to them and restore their captives" (Zephaniah 2:7). In the end, "the nations of every shore will bow in worship to Him" (Zephaniah 2:11). So stay humble, baker. Keep seeking Him today, keep your ovens ready, and don't be the cookie that bragged it couldn't burn.
